note: 2.0 fav, led strong pace, collapsed; substantial blood in trachea; trial + vet required; trainer to add hood
steward_comment: When questioned Apprentice H Y Yuen stated that her instructions were to go forward and lead. She said having regard to her instructions she rode her mount along in the early stages to ensure JEDI SPURS showed sufficient pace to cross runners to its inside. She said after obtaining a margin in advance of HAPPY PEGASUS in the early stages she then commenced to restrain her mount when she was satisfied that JEDI SPURS would be able to lead as instructed. She said as she commenced to restrain her mount approaching the 1000 Metres JEDI SPURS raced keenly and would not respond to her efforts to set a slower pace. She said making the turn leaving the 900 Metres as she applied more pressure to steady the horse to set a more sustainable pace JEDI SPURS became unbalanced when it got its head up and shifted out and from this point she was unable to control the horse in the lead. She added that soon after entering the Home Straight JEDI SPURS came under pressure before giving ground noticeably over the final 200 Metres. Trainer D A Hayes advised the horse had pleased him leading into the race and was of the opinion JEDI SPURS raced too keenly, particularly when ridden along in the early stages to go forward. He added that he would now place a hood on the horse for its next race start and use the services of a senior rider. A veterinary inspection immediately following the race which included an endoscopic examination showed a substantial amount of blood in the horse’s trachea. The performance of JEDI SPURS was considered disappointing. Before being allowed to race again, JEDI SPURS will be required to perform to the satisfaction of the Stewards in a barrier trial and be subjected to an official veterinary examination. Sent for sampling post-race.

note: raced wide without cover; bumped with Flash Current
steward_comment: Near the 400 Metres was bumped by FLASH CURRENT which attempted to shift out. When questioned K Teetan stated that his instructions were to settle the horse where comfortable but not to ride it along in the early stages. He said those instructions were issued as MR COOL had not finished its races off last season when ridden in a forward position. He said at its last start win on 4 October 2026 MR COOL was able to obtain a handy position without being ridden along to do so and his intention was to ride the horse in a similar manner today. He said whilst MR COOL jumped well he was of the opinion he would have had to make too much use of the horse in the early stages to cross runners to his inside and for this reason he elected to restrain his mount to attempt to obtain a position with cover behind PRESTIGE COME. He said when GENIUS BABY and GRAND PATCH improved to his inside he was unable to obtain cover and as a result was obliged to race very wide and without cover in the early stages. He said as the pace of the event was being run outside of standard time he then elected to ride MR COOL forward from the 900 Metres to cross GRAND PATCH where he then raced wide and without cover for the remainder of the middle stages. Trainer F C Lor confirmed the instructions issued and expressed satisfaction with the ride of Jockey Teetan. After considering his explanation the Stewards advised Jockey Teetan that he had made an error of judgement in the early stages in not attempting to cross runners to his inside, particularly when MR COOL had jumped well and the early and middle stages of the event were being run outside of standard time.

Near the 700 Metres was steadied when awkwardly positioned to the inside of MIGHTY STEED. The Stewards inquired into the reasons for TOP DRAGON being severely checked between PRAY FOR JUSTICE (K Teetan) and LUCKY SAM GOR (C L Chau) passing the winning post. K Teetan was found guilty of a charge of careless riding [Rule 100(1)] in that passing the winning post he allowed his mount to shift out, contributing to TOP DRAGON being severely checked between PRAY FOR JUSTICE and LUCKY SAM GOR. In all the circumstances K Teetan was issued with a severe reprimand and advised that in similar circumstances he would be expected to make a greater effort than what he did on this occasion to prevent his mounts from shifting ground. C L Chau was found guilty of a charge of careless riding [Rule 100(1)] in that passing the winning post he allowed his mount to shift in when insufficiently clear of TOP DRAGON, contributing to TOP DRAGON being severely checked between LUCKY SAM GOR and PRAY FOR JUSTICE. In issuing Jockey Chau with a severe reprimand the Stewards were mindful that LUCKY SAM GOR did shift in quickly which provided Jockey Chau with limited opportunity to straighten his mount. However, the Stewards advised Jockey Chau that he must react with more urgency in similar circumstances to correct his mounts.

After being crossed by WINNING DIAMOND approaching the 1300 Metres commenced to race keenly and was steadied to avoid WINNING DIAMOND.  When questioned Apprentice H Y Yuen stated that her instructions were to hold a handy position with cover.  She said in the early stages LOVELY MILES showed sufficient pace to hold a position behind the leader WINNING DIAMOND.  She said approaching the 1100 Metres when her mount was racing keenly she was reluctant to make use of it to prevent SUPER SICARIO from shifting in as she was concerned this would result in her mount racing too keenly.  She said as a result SUPER SICARIO was able to obtain a position in advance of LOVELY MILES and behind WINNING DIAMOND near the 1100 Metres. When questioned as the reason why her mount was obliged to race wide and without cover from the 1000 Metres, Apprentice Yuen stated that when making the turn near the 1000 Metres her mount shifted out which provided an opportunity for GOR GOR to obtain a position one-off behind SUPER SICARIO and this resulted in her mount being obliged to race wide and without cover thereafter. She further stated that after making contact with GOR GOR near the 550 Metres her mount shifted out which resulted in TELECOM POWER then improving to her inside and LOVELY MILES being obliged to race very wide making the Home Turn.  Trainer P F Yiu confirmed the instructions were consistent with previous instructions he issued at the horse’s most recent starts.  The Stewards advised Apprentice Yuen that she had made two errors of judgement in the early stages firstly near the 1100 Metres by not making a greater effort to hold her position behind WINNING DIAMOND to prevent SUPER SICARIO from shifting in and secondly near the 1000 Metres by permitting her mount to shift out to a three wide position which afforded GOR GOR the opportunity to obtain a position one-off following SUPER SICARIO.  She was further advised that whilst acknowledging her inexperience as an apprentice jockey in future she would be expected to show better judgement than what she did during the early stages of this race.  A veterinary inspection immediately following the race found that horse to have sustained a laceration to the right hind cannon.

H Bentley stated that after obtaining a handy position behind LOVELY MILES in the early stages his mount was shuffled back in the field when LOVELY MILES did not hold its position behind the leaders. The performance of TELECOM POWER was considered disappointing.  Before being allowed to race again, TELECOM POWER will be required to perform to the satisfaction of the Stewards in a barrier trial and be subjected to an official veterinary examination.  Sent for sampling post-race.

A Badel was advised to exercise more care.  H Bentley was severely reprimanded.  Near the 800 Metres became unbalanced when bumped by SUPERB SPIRIT which shifted out.  Raced very wide and without cover for the majority of the event.
Jumped only fairly.  Sent for sampling post-race.
Jumped awkwardly and made contact with the left side of its starting gate.

After the race an endoscopic examination was conducted on MAJESTIC VALOUR at the request of Trainer C S Shum.  The Veterinary Surgeon said this examination showed a substantial amount of blood in the horse’s trachea.  Before being allowed to race again, MAJESTIC VALOUR will be subjected to an official veterinary examination.  Sent for sampling post-race.

Blundered near the 850 Metres.  Near the 600 Metres commenced to race keenly and as a result got its head up when being checked to avoid YOUNG ARCHER.  In this incident CITY GOLD BANNER shifted out and made heavy contact with GRAND EAGLE.
Raced wide and without cover for the majority of the event.
Jumped only fairly.  Blundered near the 850 Metres and again near the 500 Metres.
Jumped only fairly.
Apprentice H Y Yuen stated that it was not the intention to lead but her mount jumped well and showed superior pace and led without being pressured to do so.
Jumped only fairly.
Bumped at the start.  Near the 900 Metres was steadied to avoid MUGEN.  BEAUTY ALLIANCE was then obliged to race wide and without cover thereafter.

Shifted out at the start and made contact with BEAUTY ALLIANCE.  Near the 900 Metres was briefly crowded by MUGEN which shifted in.  A veterinary inspection immediately following the race did not show any significant findings.

Approaching the winning post became unbalanced when crowded between ONLY U and FORTUNE KINGO. K Teetan stated that from his wide barrier he was instructed to ride the horse in a midfield position if possible. Trainer W K Mo confirmed the instructions issued.

From a wide barrier was shifted across behind runners in the early stages. Held up between the 300 Metres and 100 Metres. When improving into a narrow run between CIRCUIT CENTURY and AMO ERGO SUM near the 100 Metres was steadied when crowded by AMO ERGO SUM (S Osborne) which shifted out before being corrected by its rider. S Osborne was advised to exercise more care.
Jumped awkwardly, shifted out slightly and made contact with CIRCUIT CENTURY. A veterinary inspection immediately following the race did not show any significant findings.
Jumped only fairly. Near the 300 Metres improved to the inside of AMO ERGO SUM (S Osborne) which shifted in. S Osborne was advised in similar circumstances to exercise more care.

Shortly after the start made contact with AMO ERGO SUM which shifted out slightly. A veterinary inspection immediately following the race which included an endoscopic examination showed a substantial amount of blood in the horse’s trachea. Before being allowed to race again, CIRCUIT CENTURY will be subjected to an official veterinary examination.
Shortly after the start was checked when crowded between RUSSET GLOW and FREE PONY which was taken out by KING ALLOY (R Kingscote) which shifted out. R Kingscote was advised to exercise more care.

In the middle stages raced keenly and for some distance after the 500 Metres was steadied to avoid WINNING NOW. Held up for clear running between the 300 Metres and the 200 Metres and near the 200 Metres was shifted to the inside of BEAUTY GEMINI to obtain clear running.

Shortly after the start was checked when crowded between CHILL MASTER which was taken out and NOBLE FANS which shifted in after making contact with WINNING NOW. Approaching the 1000 Metres was eased to avoid LAKESHORE HERO which shifted in. Between the 200 Metres and the 100 Metres had some difficulty obtaining clear running.

Near the 200 Metres was hampered when taken in by MAJESTIC DELIGHT. BLUE BARON then shifted in, resulting in its rider H T Mo having to correct his mount. H T Mo stated that his mount lay in throughout the event and after being taken in near the 200 Metres finished the race off only fairly. A veterinary inspection immediately following the race did not show any significant findings.

Shortly after the start was crowded by KING ALLOY which shifted out. Near the 200 Metres was steadied when crowded by BLUE BARON (H T Mo) which, after being taken in by MAJESTIC DELIGHT (C L Chau), then shifted in and away from MAJESTIC DELIGHT when being corrected by Jockey Mo. C L Chau was advised to exercise more care and to ensure there is sufficient room to improve. Held up on the Home Turn. J Orman reported that after being crowded near the 200 Metres his mount was unable to finish its race off as a result of the interference. A veterinary inspection immediately following the race did not show any significant findings.

A Badel stated that his mount was able to lead the event but failed to respond to his riding in the Home Straight and was disappointing. He added that his mount may not have been suited by the early stages being run slightly inside of standard time. A veterinary inspection immediately following the race did not show any significant findings.
Bumped at the start. Raced wide and without cover for the majority of the event. Sent for sampling post-race.
Jumped awkwardly.
Jumped awkwardly and shortly after the start made contact with PRIVATE WEALTH. Near the 800 Metres shifted out when being steadied to avoid PRIVATE WEALTH. In the middle stages raced keenly.

Near the 800 Metres was steadied when crowded between NEW POWER and CALIFORNIA BAY which shifted out when being steadied to avoid PRIVATE WEALTH. A veterinary inspection immediately following the race did not show any significant findings.

Bumped shortly after the start. After being crossed by ARGENTO OCEAN near the 1100 Metres commenced to race keenly. As a result PRIVATE WEALTH improved to the inside of ARGENTO OCEAN and then was checked when left without sufficient room. PRIVATE WEALTH then continued to race keenly throughout the early stages and near the 900 Metres, when racing keenly, shifted out and made contact with ARGENTO OCEAN. As a result ARGENTO OCEAN and its rider B Avdulla became unbalanced, resulting in ARGENTO OCEAN shifting in and crowding the running of PRIVATE WEALTH. A warning was placed on the racing manners of PRIVATE WEALTH. A veterinary inspection immediately following the race did not show any significant findings.
Jumped only fairly. From the outside barrier was shifted across behind runners in the early stages.

Prior to the running of the event Trainer P C Ng confirmed that from a wide barrier he had instructed for the horse to be ridden in a conservative manner in the early stages to offset the wide barrier. From a wide barrier was shifted across behind runners in the early stages. Held up for clear running making the Home Turn.
Jumped only fairly.
Raced wide and without cover for the majority of the event. A veterinary inspection immediately following the race did not show any significant findings.

Made contact with a rail on entering the Parade Ring, was examined by the Veterinary Officer and passed suitable to race. On jumping was bumped by TAKE ACTION which shifted in. Approaching the 1400 Metres was steadied when crowded by AKERMANIS GOLD which was taken in by SURE JOYFUL (Apprentice H Y Yuen) which shifted in before being corrected. Apprentice Yuen was reprimanded.

Prior to the running of the event Trainer P F Yiu advised that he had instructed Apprentice H Y Yuen to hold an on-pace position but not necessarily lead. Apprentice Yuen could offer no excuse for her mount’s disappointing performance. A veterinary inspection immediately following the race did not show any significant findings.

Jumped awkwardly. E C W Wong stated that he was instructed to ride the horse in a conservative manner in the early stages. He said when unable to obtain cover GENERAL REDWOOD was obliged to race wide and without cover for the majority of the event. Trainer C S Shum confirmed the instructions issued.

Shifted in on jumping and was bumped. S Osborne could offer no excuse for the horse’s failure to run on in the Home Straight. A veterinary inspection immediately following the race did not show any significant findings.
Jumped only fairly. A veterinary inspection immediately following the race did not show any significant findings.
Near the 800 Metres shifted in towards COUNTRY PRIDE and was steadied. Raced wide and without cover for the majority of the event.

Making the Home Turn was held up for clear running. Near the 350 Metres improved into a narrow run between FLOW RIDER and WITHOUT RHYME when WITHOUT RHYME shifted out slightly. When WITHOUT RHYME then shifted back in THUNDER PRINCE was steadied when crowded. Over the concluding stages was held up behind TOP TO SKY which was giving ground. B Avdulla stated that his instructions were to settle the horse where comfortable depending on how it jumped. He said when his mount jumped only fairly it settled back in the field. Trainer J Richards confirmed the instructions issued.

Near the 800 Metres was steadied when momentarily crowded by INVICTUS which shifted in when being corrected by its rider. Near the 400 Metres was eased when momentarily crowded between INVICTUS and FORERUNNER which shifted out.
Raced wide and without cover for the majority of the event.
E C W Wong could offer no excuse for his mount not finishing the race off in the Home Straight. A veterinary inspection immediately following the race did not show any significant findings.
Jumped only fairly.

The tongue tie was replaced at the Start. In the middle stages raced keenly and approaching the 800 Metres got its head up when being steadied to avoid AURORA PATCH. Approaching the 400 Metres, when racing keenly, shifted out and made contact with ELITE GOLF. C Y Ho reported that when placed under pressure in the Home Straight his mount did not respond to his riding and raced in a disappointing manner. A veterinary inspection immediately following the race did not show any significant findings.

Shortly after the start was steadied when crowded between LUCRATIVE EIGHT and SPEEDY SMARTIE. After being crossed by LEADING AGILITY approaching the 600 Metres raced keenly and was steadied to avoid LEADING AGILITY. Bumped near the 400 Metres. A veterinary inspection immediately following the race did not show any significant findings.
From the 900 Metres commenced a forward move and was obliged to race wide and without cover thereafter. Sent for sampling post-race.
Raced wide and without cover until near the 700 Metres.

Approaching the finish of the event was steadied when crowded between MISTER DAPPER (B Avdulla) which shifted out and SHOOTING TO TOP which was taken in by POPE CODY (A Badel). B Avdulla and A Badel were advised to exercise more care.

Shortly after the start was crowded by FIVEFORTWO which shifted out. Near the 1000 Metres was bumped by HYMNBOOK which shifted out when racing keenly. Over the concluding stages could not be ridden out when positioned close to CHINA WIN.

In the early stages raced keenly and approaching the 1400 Metres was steadied to avoid FLYING FORTUNE for some distance. Near the 1000 Metres shifted out and made contact with RISING PHOENIX. H Bentley advised that the horse raced too keenly during the race and as a result was unable to finish the race off in the Home Straight. A veterinary inspection immediately following the race which included an endoscopic examination showed a substantial amount of blood in the horse’s trachea. Before being allowed to race again, HYMNBOOK will be subjected to an official veterinary examination. Sent for sampling post-race.

Shortly after the start was steadied when crowded between RISING PHOENIX and FALLON which shifted in. Near the 550 Metres was bumped by FALLON which shifted out. E C W Wong stated that after being crowded shortly after the start his mount settled further back than intended. He said CALL ME MAGNIFIQUE raced keenly throughout the early and middle stages and as a consequence did not run on in the Home Straight. A veterinary inspection immediately following the race did not show any significant findings. Before being allowed to race again, CALL ME MAGNIFIQUE will be subjected to an official veterinary examination.

Shifted in approaching the 1500 Metres and was bumped. Passing the 300 Metres was hampered when bumped by FORTUNATE SON which shifted out. Z Purton reported that his mount, which was having its first race start at Happy Valley, appeared to shy at the shadows on the track near the 1050 Metres and again near the 800 Metres.

E C W Wong stated that the intention was to hold a more forward position. He said HELENE FEELING jumped only fairly and then failed to show sufficient pace in the early stages to hold a more forward position despite being ridden along.

Jumped only fairly, shifted out and made contact with PACKING ANGEL. Approaching the 1500 Metres was bumped by BRAVEFIELD which shifted in. C Y Ho reported that his mount travelled satisfactorily during the event. He said after making contact with BRAVEFIELD entering the Home Straight his mount finished the race off only fairly thereafter. A veterinary inspection immediately following the race did not show any significant findings. Sent for sampling post-race.
Lowered its head as the start was being effected and as a result was slow to begin. Before being allowed to race again, AWESOME FLUKE will be required to perform satisfactorily in a stalls test.

A Badel reported that his mount was disadvantaged by being obliged to race wide and without cover of the majority of the event. A veterinary inspection immediately following the race did not show any significant findings.
